headline: Late November through February offers peak Palearctic migrant diversity across East Africa
summary: Palearctic migrants arrive in East Africa from late October, with peak numbers and diversity from late November through February. Early migrants (September-October) include raptors and some warblers, but many species do not reach full numbers until December. By March, return migration begins and plumage deteriorates. For maximum migrant species counts, target December-January when both European and Asian breeding birds are established in African wintering quarters.

assumptions.text: Different migrant species arrive over a 6-8 week window, not simultaneously.
December-January represents peak migrant diversity before any species begin return movement.
Arrival timing varies by 2-3 weeks between northern Kenya and southern Tanzania.

gains: December-January: Maximum migrant species present simultaneously
November-December: Many migrants still in fresh non-breeding plumage
Early rains bring insect hatches that concentrate migrants at feeding sites
Migrant raptors (steppe eagle, Montagu's harrier) easier in this window
losses: December-January coincides with peak holiday pricing
Green season conditions may complicate access to some sites
Some migrants are passage-only (September/April) and missed in mid-winter
Warblers in non-breeding plumage present identification challenges

change_conditions: If raptor migration is the focus, September-October in northern Kenya (Tsavo) is optimal.
If avoiding crowds matters, early November or late February offer 80% of migrants with fewer tourists.
If combining with calving season viewing, January-February in Tanzania serves both interests.
If specific passage migrants are targets, research their exact East African timing.
